Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Raj: Raj here. Sorry for the slight delay, been in meetings earlier.
[00:09] Sofia: Sofia on my side.
[00:11] Ben: Ben, infra.
[00:13] Liam: Liam from Redwood, hi all.
[00:15] Maya: Awesome. I'll frame the agenda: renewal numbers, region add, on-prem pilot scoping, and then technical concerns. Sound good?
[00:22] Raj: Yep, go ahead.
[00:24] Maya: Great. So first, renewal. You're currently on the mid-tier committed plan at 4k tokens/sec equivalent, right? We had you on a 12-month term that ends in September. You're looking to bump that to 12k tokens/sec equivalent to support the new triage workflow in Q4, plus an EU region for latency. Is that still the ask?
[00:41] Raj: That's correct. The new service will need low tail latency for synchronous responses, and EU residency for a subset of PHI workloads. We want a committed, predictable cost model.
[00:50] Sofia: Also need ability to route only PHI to private VPC/on-prem. Not all traffic goes there, just a small percentage, but it's sensitive. We want to avoid double egress charges if possible.
[01:02] Ben: For the VPC, we have strict firewall rules and an existing KMS setup. We need to understand KMS/HSM integration, key rotation, and audit log retention.
[01:11] Liam: Right, we can integrate with customer-managed KMS; Redwood supports external KMS and HSM via our private deployment path. There are two flavors: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra) with VPC peering, or Redwood Private which is customer-managed control plane. The former is faster to get online, the latter gives you complete network separation.
[01:28] Raj: What's the latency tradeoff between dedicated vs private? Our users expect p95 < 250ms on 512-token generations.
[01:36] Liam: Under typical loads, Dedicated in-region hits ~180-230ms p95 for 512 tokens depending on model and batching. Private can be a bit higher initially because of the extra network hops if deployed on-prem, but if you colocate in the same datacenter and we tune batching + kernel selection you'll often see comparable numbers. There's some variability though — the KV cash (KV cache) warms up and that matters for hot sessions.
[01:57] Ben: You said KV cash? I think you mean KV cache, yeah. How long to warm?
[02:02] Liam: Sorry, yes, KV cache. Warm depends on your session stickiness; if you have long conversations with the same user the cache is warm in minutes. For short-lived sessions we rely more on batching and prefix caching. We'll share some recommendations for TTL and sticky routing.
[02:20] Raj: Ok. On region add — EU: do you have a guaranteed failover plan if EU capacity is saturated? We can't have outages during peak.
[02:30] Maya: We can set routing policies: primary EU with fallback to a compatible model in US with lower cost tier, or to Dedicated fallback pool. We recommend a canary/gradual rollout per traffic slice to validate before 100% cutover. If you want an SLA-backed path we can include Dedicated capacity reserved for failover.
[02:47] Sofia: Egress is a big cost factor. How do we avoid paying for data twice if we're routing PHI across regions?
[02:54] Liam: Two levers: keep PHI in-region via Private or on-prem, or if you must cross regions, we can set up region-local pre/post-processing to minimize payload size and use server-side compression. Also the billing can be structured to reflect committed ingress/egress offsets in the quote — we'll put those options in the cost annex.
[03:14] Raj: What about SOC 2 and other compliance artifacts? We need SOC2 Type II, pen test reports and network diagrams.
[03:21] Maya: We'll share the security pack — SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, encryption-in-transit at TLS1.3, encryption-at-rest, audit log screenshots, SAML SSO guide. For Redwood Private we can add KMS integration guides and HSM vendor notes. I will send via secure share after this call.
[03:38] Ben: For on-prem pilot, we need an ops checklist: ports, VPN, CIDR ranges, and expected handshake procedures.
[03:45] Liam: I'll prep an on-prem checklist and an initial bench harness for you to validate latency and throughput end-to-end. It will be a small load test with realistic ratelimit profiles. We'll need a sample traffic profile from you — peaks per minute and token distribution — so we size batching/instances correctly.
[04:03] Raj: We can provide last quarter's traffic histograms and a sample of spike events.
[04:07] Maya: Perfect. On pricing, quick note: bump to 12k committed with a 12-month term gives you a 14% discount vs monthly on-demand; adding EU region reserved capacity is an incremental charge. We'll include burst credits for burst windows so you're not throttled during rare peaks.
[04:23] Sofia: Can we add a clause for mid-term scale? We may need to increase commitment after 3 months — want flexibility.
[04:29] Maya: Yes — we can include a mid-term amendment that allows a one-time commitment increase with a pro-rated credit applied to the remaining term. We'll mark it in the quote.
[04:36] Ben: Network question: For VPC peering with Dedicated, how are IP rotations handled? We have strict egress whitelisting.
[04:44] Liam: We support static egress IP ranges for Dedicated peering; you can whitelist them. For Private/on-prem we don't impose egress; you host in your network. For managed Private in a customer VPC we provide a short list of endpoints and recommend strict IAM roles.
[04:58] Raj: Regarding data retention: we need logs for 1 year and ability to export audit logs to our SIEM. Can Redwood do that?
[05:06] Maya: Yes, audit log export is available. We can push to your S3 or syslog endpoints, and retention can be set. We'll detail the steps in the security pack.
[05:15] Sofia: Ok good. For the on-prem pilot timeline — we want to start in August, two-week bench, then a canary in late August. Is that realistic?
[05:24] Liam: If we start prep this month (July) and you share traffic profile and infra contacts, we can get bench harness ready by the week of August 10th. Two-week test + tuning sounds fine, canary late August is realistic.
[05:35] Raj: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[05:37] Maya: SOC2 docs we can provide fast. The longer lead might be networking changes on your side and KMS approvals. Also if you go full Private on-prem we need a short access window to install the runtime; that takes coordination with your security and networking teams.
[05:52] Ben: We'll need an internal change window for that.
[05:54] Liam: We'll provide a step-by-step runbook and a rollback plan. We'll also instrument tracing hooks so you can correlate requests through your infra.
[06:05] Raj: Ok great. A quick question about model variants — can we pin different models for PHI vs non-PHI to reduce cost?
[06:12] Liam: Yes. You can route PHI to a smaller, more deterministic model with quantization, and route high-throughput non-PHI to a larger open model. Our routing policies and rollout allow per-route model pinning and automatic fallback. We'll show examples in the config doc.
[06:27] Sofia: Any limitations on function calling / tool integrations in Private? We rely on a medical knowledge base connector for some calls.
[06:35] Liam: Function calling works same across modes; if connector touches PHI you can host that connector inside your VPC and call it from the runtime. We'll validate auth flows and token passing in the bench.
[06:45] Raj: All right. I think that covers main points. Maybe open the floor for smaller technical Qs?
[06:50] Ben: On the bench: what load generator should we use? JMeter? Fortio?
[06:54] Liam: We use a simple Python harness that mimics your token distributions; for open-source we often recommend Fortio + a small wrapper. We'll share the harness repo.
[07:05] Sofia: About pricing annex: include explicit numbers for committed throughput, burst credits, EU reserved pricing, and one-time on-prem pilot fees.
[07:13] Maya: Will do. I'll include a clear table in the quote.
[07:18] Raj: Great. Anything else?
[07:20] Maya: Quick recap then next steps.

Redwood sends quote + security pack, Liam preps bench harness & on-prem checklist, Ben shares VPC details and traffic profile.
